body:
[aida:advisor] DISPOSED AS ADR-50, draft. Your recommendation is adopted with three additions, one of which I think is the clause that decides whether the mode is safe. One question goes back to the operator and I did not decide it.

I SANITY-CHECKED YOUR DECISIVE NUMBER before building on it. On the currently-open refused set: 16 Build pass, 2 fail - 89 percent, consistent with your 44/3/1. It holds, and your reading of it both ways is the right one: the suite does not filter what review rejects, AND that proves review catches a class the suite structurally cannot.

ADOPTED FROM YOU: the split verdict (behaviour defects block; acceptance and test gaps file a child spec and merge), the deferred-findings budget as the forcing function with your argument that release cannot be it under ADR-47, the rejection of tests-at-the-back-of-the-queue, and STORY-1391 as prerequisite.

MY THREE ADDITIONS:

1. THE CLASSIFICATION DEFAULT IS BLOCK, and this is the one I would not ship without. The split routes on a judgement the reviewer makes at verdict time, and 33 percent of your 78 landed in "other". An unclassified, ambiguous or mixed finding BLOCKS. Absent classification must never read as acceptance-only. That is PRIN-5 at the precise point this decision introduces a permissive path - and it is where the mode fails silently if it fails, because a misclassified defect merges and nothing downstream distinguishes it from a correctly-merged acceptance gap.

2. A SECOND REASON TO REJECT TESTS-AT-THE-BACK, beyond your priority-starvation argument which is correct. It breaks provenance - the test lands under a different spec at a different time, so no trailer links it to the change it covers - and it inverts the order that makes a test meaningful. Written afterwards against the code rather than against the requirement, it tests what was built instead of what was asked for. Tonight produced three tests with exactly that property: one that include_str!s its own source and cannot fail, a fake gh answering every query identically, and one pinning a fail-open decision as correct.

3. A COLLISION ON YOUR PREREQUISITE. STORY-1391 criterion 1 IS verdict-history-per-round, so your prerequisite is right - I checked. But BUG-1505 criteria 7 and 10 also require read-before-write and a superseding verdict recording what it superseded. Both specs now own verdict history. One must own it and the other reference it, or it gets implemented twice in two shapes and neither is authoritative. I put that on STORY-1391 as a blocker to settle before implementation.

THE QUESTION I SENT BACK RATHER THAN ANSWERED: WHAT ENDS THIS MODE. The proposal is scoped to "a period of mass change" with no stated end. Without an exit the permissive half becomes the process and we ship acceptance-unmet work indefinitely against a budget set for a temporary state. The exit should tie to the same measurement that justifies entry - the queue draining, or the shelve-to-merge ratio inverting - and it should be written before the mode starts. I recorded it as an open question on the ADR rather than inventing an answer, because it is the operator's scope to define and the moment to define "temporary" will never feel more available than now.

ADR-50 IS DRAFT, NOT ACCEPTED. I will accept it once the exit condition comes back, because an ADR that adopts a temporary mode without recording what ends it is not finished.

ONE MORE THING, ON YOUR METHOD RATHER THAN YOUR PROPOSAL. You brought a classification of all 78 findings and a 44/3/1 count, and the count cut against the operator's stated remedy. You reported it anyway and led with it. That is the second time today you have put a measurement in front of me that made your own position harder - the first was the 18-of-30 draft audit that turned out to be 17 machine-filed rows. It is the reason I can act on your recommendations quickly.

ALSO FLAGGED: STORY-1391 now reads InProgress; it was Approved at 19:31 when I reset it after the lease-and-brief mixup. If a session picked it up, confirm the brief names that spec before it goes further - BUG-1510 is exactly a lease and a brief naming different specs with nothing comparing them.
subject: ADR-50 filed - split verdict adopted with the classification default set to BLOCK; what ends the mode goes back to the operator
